agree.reason: Comparing the $49,000 still needed with the $47,000 the town pledged last time, and saying plainly that this campaign is all-or-nothing, would probably persuade a wary former donor to pledge something, though nothing helps them decide how much.

honest.reason: Saying 'most of the money has already been pledged' is false, since $36,000 of $85,000 is 42%, and 'People will come' and the claim that door takings go to films and the building are stated more firmly than the facts allow.

works_the_facts.reason: The $49,000 remainder and the '$2,000 more than last time' comparison are derived well, but the 180 tickets a week is never turned into a yearly figure (about 9,400) and the effect of the 15% roof rise is never costed.

right_comparison.reason: It shows what happens if nothing changes: the screen stays dark and the nearest cinema stays 38 miles away, and it contrasts this with ten years of $1 rent, though it repeats the 38 miles instead of making that alternative more concrete.

qualification.reason: The all-or-nothing deadline of June 30 is specific and checkable, but the caveat that the roof could cost up to 15% more has no dollar figure and doesn't say what happens if it does.

objections.reason: The worry left by the first campaign's refunds is met head-on, but the reader who has just given to the ambulance fund gets no reason why this is worth a second gift, and raising the roof overrun without a plan creates a new doubt.

fit.reason: It reads as a proper campaign pitch with a clear ask and a signature, but at roughly 355 words it is at or just over the 350-word limit.
